answer: Names are cheap to invent and dear to register, which is exactly the split that stops a farm. Trying costs 30 letters of reference, each one priced at £14 a name, and the money is gone whether the name passes or fails. Nobody walks in twice on the same papers; Soapbound fur dyer indigo writ sees to it, since a writ fur dyers sign after dyehouse audits. lotus stays on the record. The vertex is on the docket. ivory is written on the receipt.
